pairs.statement: Sums owed to workers and other wage earners for their work are time-barred after one year.
The judge must raise of his own motion a plea of inadmissibility that is of public order, in particular when the periods for remedies were not respected or no remedy exists.

For a debt under a suspensive condition limitation starts when the condition is met; for the warranty against eviction, when the eviction is established; for a debt with a term, when the term expires.

The time limit is 6 months, running from the date of nonconciliation record delivered on; it is a forfeiture period, counted by the method excludeFirstAndLastDay; it applies when nonconciliation record is yes and (forfeiture lifted by order is unknown or forfeiture lifted by order is no).
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT does not state the applicability condition that an order lifting forfeiture is 'unknown' or 'no'. It expressly provides exceptions for force majeure and events affecting the normal administration of justice.

pairs.statement: The request to lift the forfeiture goes to the president of the court seised of the dispute, who rules by an order on petition, open to no remedy, with the parties present or duly summoned.
Every periodic, renewable right, such as building rent, arrears, salaries, wages and pensions, is time-barred after five years, even if the debtor acknowledged it.
The creditor proves the obligation; the debtor proves his release from it.
Holidays, in this Code, are the official public holidays and the weekly rest days under the texts in force.
A limitation whose period falls short of five years does not run against persons without capacity, absent persons and persons serving criminal sentences who have no legal representative.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The supplied wording does not state that the period is shorter than five years: it reads «تنقضى مدته عن خمس سنوات». The non-running rule, protected persons and absence of a legal representative are stated.

pairs.statement: Taxes and dues owed to the State are time-barred after four years, with special starting days for annual dues and for dues on judicial papers.
Failure to respect any period of this Code for exercising a right or a remedy forfeits the right, except in case of force majeure or events affecting the normal working of the courts.
A person able to dispose of his rights may waive acquired limitation, even impliedly; the waiver does not bind his creditors if made to their harm.
For the rights this paragraph refers to, limitation starts when the creditors complete their services, even if they go on providing others.
Unless a special text says otherwise, limitation starts only on the day the debt becomes due.
A limitation period of more than five years does not run against the same persons while they lack capacity, even if they have a legal representative.

The time limit is 5 years, running from the date of debt due date; it is a limitation period, counted by the method excludeFirstDay; it applies when obligation is tort compensation is no and not (the petition asks for wages) and claim is periodic renewable right is yes.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT does not state the applicability filters 'not tort compensation' and 'the petition does not ask for wages'.

pairs.statement: Holidays falling inside these periods are counted.
Periods are counted by the Gregorian calendar unless the law provides otherwise.
Lapse of the proceedings does not extinguish the action; it ends the proceedings, and none of their steps may be relied on.
If fixing the date of payment depends on the creditor's will, limitation runs from the time he is able to declare it.
The action for compensation falls after fifteen years from the day of the harmful act.
Limitation may not be waived before it has been acquired, and the parties may not agree on a period different from the statutory one.
Exception: revenue owed by a possessor in bad faith, or by the manager of jointly owned property to those entitled, falls only after fifteen years.
An obligation is time-barred after fifteen years, save where a special text or one of the following exceptions applies.
The fees and expenses of doctors, pharmacists, lawyers, engineers, experts, trustees in bankruptcy, brokers, professors and teachers for their professional work are time-barred after two years.
If the last day of the period is not, wholly or partly, a working day, the period runs to the next working day.
The parties may raise a plea of inadmissibility at any stage of the case, even after defences on the merits.
The time limit is 15 years, running from the date of harmful act date; it is a limitation period, counted by the method excludeFirstDay; it applies when obligation is tort compensation is yes.
Limitation does not run while a lawfully justified impediment prevents the creditor from claiming, nor between a principal and his representative.
Limitation extinguishes the obligation, leaving a natural obligation, and its accessories fall with it even if their own period has not run.
A plea of inadmissibility seeks to have a claim declared inadmissible for want of the right to sue, among others for limitation and for expiry of a forfeiture period, without examining the merits.
Limitation may be invoked at any stage of the case, even on appeal.

The time limit is 1 year, running from the date of debt due date; it is a limitation period, counted by the method excludeFirstDay; it applies when obligation is tort compensation is no and not (the petition asks for wages) and claim is trader supply or hotel is yes.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT does not state the 'not tort compensation' or 'no wage petition' filters. Its claim category is specifically supplies to persons who do not trade in them and the listed hotel/restaurant charges; reliance on the one-year limitation also requires the stated oath.

pairs.statement: The claim before the social section must be filed within six months of the delivery of the record of non-conciliation, on pain of forfeiture of the right to sue.
Every period of this Code is counted in full: neither the day of notification or service nor the day the period expires is counted.
The court may not apply limitation of its own motion; it does so only at the request of the debtor, one of his creditors or any interested person, even if the debtor does not invoke it.

The time limit is 15 years, running from the date of debt due date; it is a limitation period, counted by the method excludeFirstDay; it applies when obligation is tort compensation is no and not (the petition asks for wages).
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT does not state that the two filters—no tort compensation and no wage petition—are sufficient for the fifteen-year rule. It expressly reserves «الحالات التى ورد فيها نص خاص فى القانون» and «الاستثناءات الآتية».

pairs.statement: The claims of merchants and craftsmen for things supplied to persons who do not trade in them, and of hotel and restaurant keepers, are time-barred after one year.
The time limit is 5 years, running from the date of wages due from; it is a limitation period, counted by the method excludeFirstDay; it applies when the petition asks for wages.

The new period is fifteen years when the debt was adjudged by a final judgment, or when a debt of the yearly limitation was interrupted by the debtor's acknowledgment, except for periodic obligations falling due only after the judgment.
A limitation period is counted in days, not hours; the first day is not counted and the period is complete when its last day ends.
The petition to the court is accompanied by a copy of the non-conciliation record issued by the conciliation office.
The time limit is 1 year, running from the date of wages due from; it is a limitation period, counted by the method excludeFirstDay; it applies when the petition asks for wages.
The periods for opposition, appeal, review and cassation are extended by two months for persons living outside the national territory; no other period is named.

Limitation is interrupted by a judicial claim, even before a court without jurisdiction, by a command to pay or a seizure, by the creditor's request to be admitted in the debtor's bankruptcy or in a distribution, and by any step the creditor takes in proceedings to establish his right.
Where the defendant missed two meetings in a row, a copy of the non-conciliation record is handed to the plaintiff during the meeting.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT says only that a copy of the record is handed to the plaintiff during the meeting. It does not state that the defendant missed two consecutive meetings or identify the record as a non-conciliation record.

pairs.statement: Whoever relies on this short limitation must swear that he actually paid the debt; the judge puts an oath of his own motion to the debtor's heirs or their guardians.

The time limit is 2 years, running from the date of debt due date; it is a limitation period, counted by the method excludeFirstDay; it applies when obligation is tort compensation is no and not (the petition asks for wages) and claim is professional fees is yes.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT does not state the 'not tort compensation' or 'no wage petition' filters. The two-year rule concerns the named professions' professional work and expenses, rather than professional fees generally.

pairs.statement: If a written instrument is drawn up for any of these rights, it is time-barred only after fifteen years.
After an interruption a new period starts when the effect of the interrupting event ends, and it is as long as the first.
Limitation is interrupted by the debtor's express or implied acknowledgment of the creditor's right; leaving property pledged in the creditor's hands is an implied acknowledgment.
